2027-03-11.title: Fifth Thursday of the Great Fast
2027-03-11.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-03-11.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-03-11.verse: for, while physical training is of some value, godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.
theo: Paul writes to Timothy, his young co-worker in Ephesus, as a coach writes to an athlete. The Greek world loved its gymnasium, and Paul borrows its language: “Train yourself in godliness, for, while physical training is of some value, godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.” He does not despise the body's training; he simply sets it in its place. The body's fitness serves this life; godliness, eusebeia, a life turned reverently toward God, serves this life and the next. Like any training, it needs daily practice, a coach, and the willingness to be tired. Before dawn in many Kerala villages the young men of the kalari stretch and leap and repeat the same movements until they become second nature; no one becomes a master of kalaripayattu by reading about it. The Great Fast is the Church's season of training: the same prayers each morning and evening, the same small refusals at the table, the same Way of the Cross each Friday, until the soul learns new reflexes. Paul also warns Timothy to “Have nothing to do with profane myths and old wives' tales”, idle stories that fill the mind and starve the soul; today they come to us through the endless scrolling of our phones. And he gives the reason for all the effort: “For to this end we toil and struggle, because we have our hope set on the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe.” We do not train to impress anyone. We train because we hope.

In the Gospel Jesus takes the Twelve aside and tells them, for the third time in Luke, what is waiting at the end of the road: “See, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything that is written about the Son of Man by the prophets will be accomplished. For he will be handed over to the Gentiles; and he will be mocked and insulted and spat upon. After they have flogged him, they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise again.” Every word is clear. And yet Luke tells us three times over that they did not grasp it: “But they understood nothing about all these things; in fact, what he said was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what was said.” They had walked with him for years, seen his miracles, heard his parables, and still the Cross made no sense to them. The very next scene in Luke is a blind beggar at Jericho who cries out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”, and receives his sight (Luke 18:38). Those who walked beside Jesus could not see; the blind man by the road could. Only after Easter would the risen Lord open their minds to understand the Scriptures. In ten days we enter the Great Week. We too may know every word of the Passion story and still not understand it. Let us ask, like the beggar of Jericho, for eyes to see that the road up to Jerusalem is the road to glory.
outline: Ask: what am I training myself for this Lent?
The third foretelling of the Passion.
Asking for eyes to see the Cross.
live: Choose one spiritual exercise, the same each day until Easter: a psalm, a decade of the Rosary, ten minutes of the Gospel, and do not miss a day.
Keep your phone away for one hour each evening this week, and give that hour to prayer or to your family.
2027-03-11.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you set your face to go up to Jerusalem, knowing that you would be mocked, insulted, flogged and killed, and that on the third day you would rise. Train us in godliness through the discipline of this Great Fast, and set our hope on the living God. Open the eyes of our hearts, as you opened the eyes of the blind man at Jericho, so that we may understand your Cross and follow you to your glory. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is the school in which Christ trains us in godliness: day after day the same words and gestures form our hearts, until we understand the mystery of his Passion and Resurrection that we celebrate.

quick: Paul: train yourself in godliness; it holds promise for this life and the next.
Jesus foretells his Passion and Resurrection for the third time.
The disciples understood nothing; let us ask for eyes to see the meaning of the Cross.
2027-03-11.action: Choose one daily spiritual exercise and keep it every day until Easter.
2027-03-11.question: What am I really training myself for?

family.explain: Jesus told his friends that in Jerusalem people would hurt him and kill him, but that on the third day he would rise again. His friends did not understand. Soon we will remember these days in Holy Week. Let us ask Jesus to help us understand how much he loves us.
family.intention: We pray that our family may keep Holy Week well, and understand Jesus' love.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one good habit we can practise every day together until Easter?”

illus: A schoolboy in Kannur joined the kalari near his house during the summer holidays. On the first morning the gurukkal made him do nothing but stand in the basic stance until his legs shook. On the tenth morning, the same. He complained to his grandfather, who had trained there fifty years before. The old man said: the stance is not the lesson; the stance is what makes every later lesson possible. That Lent the boy noticed that his grandfather prayed the same short prayers every morning on the veranda, without fail, and understood that this too was a stance.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you went up to Jerusalem for us. Train our hearts and open our eyes as we pray. Amen.
share: Train yourself in godliness (1 Timothy 4:7). What daily practice is forming my soul, and what is deforming it?
We have our hope set on the living God (1 Timothy 4:10). Where is my hope really set?
They understood nothing about all these things (Luke 18:34). What part of the mystery of the Cross do I still not understand?
interc: For the Church, that she may be a good school of prayer and holiness.
For catechists and teachers who train the young in faith.
For young people, that they may train their bodies and their souls.
For those who do not understand the meaning of suffering in their lives.
For our group, that we may keep Holy Week with open eyes and hearts.
pm.close: Father, your Son went up to Jerusalem to suffer and to rise. Train us in godliness, set our hope on you, and give us light to understand his Passion, so that we may share his glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells Timothy: train yourself in godliness; physical training is of some value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come (1 Timothy 4:7–8).

The Great Fast is a season of training. The same prayers every day, the same small sacrifices at table, the same Way of the Cross each Friday: slowly they give the soul new habits. We train not to impress others, but because our hope is set on the living God.

In the Gospel Jesus tells the Twelve: we are going up to Jerusalem; the Son of Man will be mocked, insulted, spat upon, flogged and killed, and on the third day he will rise again (Luke 18:31–33). But they understood nothing (Luke 18:34).

We too can know the Passion story by heart and still not understand it. In ten days we enter the Great Week. Let us ask, like the blind man of Jericho, for eyes to see that the way of the Cross is the way to glory. Amen.
kids: Children, sportsmen practise every day to become strong. Jesus' friends also need to practise: praying every day and doing good things every day. What good thing will you practise every day until Easter?
